blocks.text: Jonk is one of the world’s most acclaimed photographers of abandoned places. For more than ten years, he has been traveling the globe in search of them. In this twelfth book, Urbex Storie s, he takes us along on his adventures through twenty true stories set in seven countries. A dog, a rifle, a knife, a punch, an alarm, a guard, the police, a fall, hide-and-seek: these are just some of the ingredients that make this book a total immersion at his side in the fascinating world of urbex. Jonk writes:

Since the spring of 2025, a lucky few have been able to join me in the wastelands on my Urbex Tours. Over periods of four to six days, in small groups of four, I offer an immersion into my work as a ruin hunter. This book is a way of taking more people with me into the very particular world of urbex, so intriguing, and so frightening for some.

With Urbex Stories , I want to reveal what lies behind my photos. Whether through searching for locations, travelling, on-site approaches, but also post-processing and the life of a photographer, I have tried to select stories that give the reader a complete panorama of my world. Of course, most of the stories focus on the visits themselves and the adventures they brought. From meeting an owner or a security guard to encountering a guard dog or wild animals, by way of experiences with weapons or narrowly avoided physical accidents, a lot happens behind an image seen on social media, in books or in exhibitions.

All of this is only part of the twenty stories told here; I’ll leave the rest be a surprise. Spoiler alert nonetheless: you’ll find a reference to American History X that still sends a chill down my spine, some decidedly unfriendly Russians met in Italy, a punch, a prostitute, an alarm, broken equipment, racism… in short, enough to make you want to join me on my Tours!

Through this book, I also hope to share my taste for old stones, and my passion for the spectacle of time passing and leaving its mark on everything. This patina of wear and decay, these markers of time gone by that I never stop citing but will write down once more here: rusted iron, peeling paint, dust, broken glass and, of course, nature taking back its place, create fabulous settings. For me, at least, and I hope for you too when you close this book.
Happy reading, and enjoy the immersion into my world!

The book can be ordered from any bookstore in France, from any online bookstore, or on the websites of Jonk or Editions Tempus Fugit for a signed or autographed copy. It contains 122 photographs taken in 8 countries.
